nodes.name: Co-MI growth on Ni foam
nodes.procedure: 2-methylimidazole (20 mmol, MI) was dissolved into deionized water (50 ml) to form solution A. Cobalt nitrate (2.5 mmol, Co(NO3)2·6H2O) was dissolved in deionized water (50 ml) to form solution B. Then solution B was poured into solution A to form solution C. Ni foam (1×2 cm2) was put into solution C. After soaking for 6 h, the Co-MI (Co-MOF) electrode was obtained. Subsequently, the electrode was rinsed with deionized water.
nodes.source_text: First, 2-methylimidazole (20 mmol, MI) was dissolved into deionized water (50 ml)... the electrode was rinsed with deionized water.

nodes.name: Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH/MI immersion
nodes.procedure: A solution was prepared by dissolving cobalt nitrate (Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 1 mmol), iron nitrate (Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 1 mmol) and an Ir3+ aqueous solution (7.14 mg ml-1, 350 μl) in a mixture of deionized water (20 ml) and ethylene glycol (10 ml). The pH value of this solution was kept at ~4.5 by adding an appropriate amount of 2 mol l-1 NaOH. Subsequently, the pre-prepared Co-MI electrode was immersed in this solution for 20 h. Following immersion, the Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH/MI was obtained and washed three times using deionized water.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Ir-containing catalysts closely resemble their Ir-free counterparts, confirming absence of Ir nanoparticles or bulk Ir metal; characteristic layered double hydroxide peaks identify CoFe hydroxides as supports.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) patterns of Ir-containing catalysts closely resemble their Ir-free counterparts, confirming the absence of Ir nanoparticles or bulk Ir metal (Fig. 2a and Supplementary Fig. 15). Characteristic layered double hydroxide peaks in the XRD patterns identify CoFe hydroxides as the supports for Ir single atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge XANES spectra show peaks shifted ~0.4 eV higher than Ir foil but lower than IrO2, suggesting Ir oxidation state between 0 and +4; linear regression refines Ir oxidation states to +1.02 for Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH/MI and +0.91 for Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ir L3-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra for both Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH/MI and Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH show similar peaks, shifted ~0.4 eV higher than Ir foil but lower than IrO2, suggesting an Ir oxidation state between 0 and +4 (refs. 14,36) (Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 16). Linear regression analysis of the first-order derivative zero further refines the Ir oxidation states to +1.02 and +0.91 for Ir/(Co,Fe)-OH/MI and Ir/(Co,Fe)-OH, respectively (Fig. 2c and Supplementary Fig. 17).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS spectra reveal Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH/MI shows peaks at 1.68 Å (Ir–O or Ir–N) and 2.68 Å (Ir–Co or Ir–Fe), implying impact of MI coordination; wavelet-transformed EXAFS supports atomic dispersion of Ir species on CoFe hydroxides with no evidence of Ir clusters or nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra reveal the nature of Ir bonds in Ir/(Co,Fe)-OH/MI, Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH, IrO2 and Ir foil (Fig. 2d). ... By contrast, Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH/MI shows a slightly shifted profile with peaks at 1.68 Å (Ir–O or Ir–N) and 2.68 Å (Ir–Co or Ir–Fe), implying an impact of MI coordination. The wavelet-transformed Ir L3-edge EXAFS spectra of Ir1/(Co,Fe)-OH/MI and Ir/(Co,Fe)-OH exhibit distinct differences compared with IrO2 and Ir foil (Fig. 2e), further supporting the atomic dispersion of Ir species on CoFe hydroxides, with no evidence of Ir clusters or nanoparticles.
